health_and_wellness.summary: John values structured fitness, preventive care, therapy, meditation, and practical stress management.
details: Plays weekly pickup basketball, hikes, and does cardio or body-weight workouts about three or four days weekly when his schedule cooperates (Q31, Q32).
Uses monthly therapy, meditation, journaling, quiet walks, screen boundaries, and sleep routines to manage generalized anxiety tendencies and work stress (Q18, Q33, Q45, Q50).
Carries stress physically through tight shoulders, stomach tension, bad sleep, and occasional tension headaches, but has no major diagnosis, broken bones, or daily chronic condition (Q31, Q33).
Sprained his ankle playing basketball last year, missed about six weeks, and did a few physical therapy sessions plus home balance and calf exercises (Q33).
Has employer health insurance, an HSA, a primary care doctor, annual visits, and generally does not forgo needed care, though scheduling, networks, copays, and opaque costs frustrate him (Q36, Q40).
Is pro-vaccination and trusts his doctor, CDC, major hospital systems, Ohio State medical sources, and public health experts who explain uncertainty clearly (Q41, Q42).

Does not smoke, drinks mostly wine or beer in moderation, watches stress-related drinking, uses marijuana only rarely in social settings, has no regular prescriptions, and does not use anxiety medication (Q38, Q39).
Helps manage family health logistics, especially his father's blood pressure and cholesterol paperwork and his mother's recovery from knee replacement surgery (Q35, Q40).

Enjoys bold red wines such as Chianti, Barolo, Zinfandel, and California cabernet with food, including steak or mushroom risotto (Q38).

summaries.demographer: John Papagno is a 36-year-old white, Italian-American man living alone in a rented one-bedroom apartment in Columbus, Ohio's 43202 area (Q08, Q11, Q84, Q88, Q89). He has a bachelor's degree in management information systems from Ohio State and works full-time as a B2B technology sales manager, placing him in a stable middle-to-upper-middle professional class position (Q16, Q65, Q90). He has never been married, has no children, and maintains close ties to parents, a sister, brother-in-law, nephew, and local friendship networks (Q05, Q07, Q84). His life-course profile shows delayed marriage or partnership, strong family embeddedness, and urban professional independence.
summaries.behavioral_economist: John is motivated by a mix of mastery, autonomy, measurable progress, and identity-consistent experiences such as art, food, travel, and sports (Q02, Q57, Q61, Q109). He uses spreadsheets, budgeting apps, automated savings, Salesforce metrics, and routines to manage uncertainty and prevent drift, though he acknowledges impulse spending on dining, travel, and art (Q03, Q57, Q61, Q62). His risk posture is moderate: he has emergency savings and can absorb a $400 shock, but housing prices, health costs, and variable sales compensation keep him cautious (Q58, Q82, Q83). Social commitment increases follow-through, especially in basketball and hiking, while stress can weaken his self-control around sleep, food, wine, and scrolling (Q32, Q38, Q50).
summaries.political_scientist: John is a consistent voter who usually supports Democrats and describes himself as center-left or pragmatic progressive (Q23, Q24, Q95, Q96). He values competent institutions, health care access, climate policy, public education, reproductive rights, voting rights, and accountable policing, while remaining skeptical of performative outrage (Q24, Q25). His response to Black Lives Matter includes listening to Black friends and coworkers, attending one peaceful march, making small donations, and applying structured fairness principles at work (Q26, Q27, Q29). He has moderate-to-high civic engagement through voting, local issue attention, and community networks, but he is not a high-intensity activist (Q23, Q29, Q30).
summaries.psychologist: John presents as conscientious, analytical, socially attuned, ambitious, and emotionally reactive, with a strong need to convert uncertainty into plans, metrics, and routines (Q15, Q18, Q45, Q65). He experiences anxiety tendencies marked by over-preparation, rumination, and physical stress, but actively uses therapy, meditation, journaling, exercise, and walks to regulate himself (Q31, Q33, Q43, Q45, Q50). His self-concept blends Midwestern practicality, Italian-American family warmth, technical competence, creative curiosity, and a desire to lead without burning people out (Q01, Q47, Q65, Q108). Relationally, he is close to family and friends but sometimes struggles to slow down enough for connection, especially when work pressure activates his controlling side (Q05, Q07, Q44, Q109).
